sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Museum SimCity L201 directly states players build a city and respond to ever-changing problems/needs depending on their decisions. L204 describes laying roads/buildings and consequences, distinguishing city management from direct hero traversal or shooting. Only slot2 states this main player activity; frozenkey2 was checked against that narrative. Other tasks are credible recognizable videogame-play categories with source-backed examples, not impossible non-game jokes. Wording uses parallel infinitive task phrases and comparable length/detail; key is not the sole coherent or composite alternative. The City name may suggest an urban setting, but urban titles need not be builders, so it does not force this particular task by grammar alone.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: В SimCity игрок строит город и отвечает на его меняющиеся проблемы и потребности. Игра не задаёт единственную цель победы: желаемый результат выбирает сам игрок.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Sentence1 accurately summarizes SimCity L201’s city-building and dynamically changing problems/needs. Sentence2 follows the same paragraph and Wright quotation: no single imposed desirable outcome, player chooses it. The wording says no single victory goal, not that optional scenarios/tasks never exist. Exactly2 sentences, names SimCity and the correct activity rather than only saying slot2 is correct.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Super Mario Bros. — боковой платформер; игрок ведёт Марио через Грибное королевство, чтобы спасти принцессу Пич.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Super Mario Bros L203 explicitly calls it a side-scrolling platformer; L204–L205 says players guide Mario through Mushroom Kingdom to save Princess Peach. The note teaches a concrete example and objective of the own platformer alternative, without attributing that hero-rescue activity to SimCity.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Pac-Man — лабиринтная аркада 1980 года: её жёлтый герой и четыре привидения стали частью массовой культуры.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Pac-Man L198 explicitly dates it to1980 and describes a maze game with yellow title character and four ghosts; L195/L199 supports mass-cultural reach. The note gives a useful actual maze-game example for this alternative, and makes no unsupported Pac-Man pellet/progression-rule claim.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Уилл Райт задумал SimCity после того, как ему понравилось играть с редактором карты в его прежней игре Raid on Bungeling Bay.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: SimCity L200 says the idea germ arose from Wright enjoying the Raid on Bungeling Bay map editor as much as the game, and his urban-growth interest then led to SimCity. The note accurately identifies designer, prior game and editor inspiration. This is additional historical information specifically about the genesis of the city-building experience beyond the asked task, not merely a generic lifespan fact or the prompt/key restated.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: В Space Invaders игрок передвигает лазерную пушку по нижней части экрана и стреляет по наступающим рядам пришельцев.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Space Invaders L202 explicitly states players move a laser cannon across the screen bottom and fire at rows of advancing aliens; L203 places the game in shooter history. The note keeps those concrete action/control facts and omits unsupported precision beyond the visible source. It is useful for the own cannon/shooting alternative, not a claim about SimCity.

absoluteLevel.ground: The question asks the basic purpose of a long-established city-simulation brand, recognizable to a broad adult PC/family-gaming cohort, not a release date, advanced city algorithm, designer biography or obscure mechanic. Building and managing a city is the broad experience; an unfamiliar adult can still compare coherent play categories rather than eliminate absurd non-game options. English City provides an accessible thematic hint without logically excluding urban action/maze games. Museum L208–L210 corroborates adult/PC/console audience breadth, but its popularity/easy-to-learn statements are contextual evidence, not alone a difficulty proof. This is an editorial judgment of the exact task and four choices.
absoluteLevel.limitations: No telemetry or human acceptance inferred; note’s deeper design-history fact is not required to answer.
